recap.text: 97 Problems take over 1st in the real standings with 247 points after a 44-point week, edging Tage Against the Machine (245), who slip to 2nd. Lord of the Rinks sit 3rd with 240 and Matthew's Team are 4th with 239, so the top four are separated by eight points.
recap.impact: We are 7 points off the lead in the real standings, close enough that one good week flips it. The real race is with 97 Problems.

recap.text: Lord of the Rinks are now the projected favourite, finishing on about 788 points to 97 Problems' 786. Title odds: Lord of the Rinks 29.1%, 97 Problems 25.6%, Tage Against the Machine 13.2%, Dom Scavuzzo 9.8%, PhilCap 8.2%.
recap.impact: Our win odds jumped from 21.0% to 29.1% this week and we passed 97 Problems for 1st in the projections. It is basically a two-horse race with them.

recap.text: Biggest movers: Tage Against the Machine climb from 5th to 3rd in the projections (10.3% to 13.2%), while PhilCap drop from 3rd to 5th (12.8% to 8.2%) and Debits & Checks fall from 4th to 6th (11.4% to 5.4%). Peter Will Probably Pick Old Guys managed only 15 points and tumble from 5th to 10th in the real standings.
recap.impact: PhilCap and Debits & Checks fading thins out the chase pack behind us. Tage are the team to watch for 3rd, but they are projected about 20 points behind us.

recap.text: Top pool scorers this week: Robert Thomas, Brock Boeser and Leon Draisaitl with 10 points each, Connor McDavid with 9, and Kirill Kaprizov, Matt Boldy, Patrick Kane and Tyler Bertuzzi with 8. Boeser has a point in 14 straight games.
recap.impact: Two of the week's top five are ours (Thomas and Kaprizov), and they did most of the lifting behind our 39-point week.

recap.text: Injuries: Nathan MacKinnon is now expected to be out about 12 weeks, Oliver Bjorkstrand is out 2 to 3 months, and Quinn Hughes will miss Minnesota's road trip. Nikolaj Ehlers (97 Problems) missed Sunday after a hit, and Anton Frondell left Saturday's game in Calgary and is day-to-day. Aleksander Barkov could return Wednesday.
recap.impact: Frondell is our lowest-projected skater, so a short absence costs little. Ehlers being hurt dents our main rival, and Barkov's return would help Sam Reinhart's line.

recap.text: Role changes on the lineup sheets: Porter Martone has moved up to the first power-play unit in Philadelphia, while Dylan Holloway in St. Louis and Anton Frondell in Chicago have dropped to the second unit.
recap.impact: Mixed for us: Martone's bump helps, Holloway's drop hurts a little, and Frondell's matters less while he is hurt.

lens.headline: Thomas and Kaprizov carry the Rinks to the top of the projections.
bullets: We are 3rd in the real standings with 240 points, 7 behind 97 Problems and 5 behind Tage Against the Machine, and projected to finish 1st on about 788 points.
Win odds rose from 21.0% to 29.1% this week, and top-3 odds from 47.6% to 60.0%.
The projected race with 97 Problems is razor thin (about 788 to 786), and Tage are about 20 points further back, so simply keeping pace with 97 Problems in the real standings is what it takes.

Robert Thomas (10 points) and Kirill Kaprizov (8) drove the week. Kaprizov, Brady Tkachuk and Roope Hintz are scoring on more of their shots than usual, so expect some cooling, while Wyatt Johnston is due for more goals. Porter Martone moved up to the top power-play unit; Dylan Holloway and Anton Frondell moved down.
Next week, watch Frondell's status, Nikolaj Ehlers' injury on the 97 Problems side, and whether Aleksander Barkov returns Wednesday alongside Sam Reinhart.

lens.headline: Kaprizov's hat trick kept you in a three-way race, now 3rd projected.
bullets: You're 16th in the real standings with 29 points, but projected to finish 3rd with about 737, and your roster still projects 1st in the pool from here on.
Win odds slipped from 18.7% to 17.1% since last week's recap, and top-3 odds from 40% to 39%, as Dom Scavuzzo jumped past you from 4th to 1st projected.
The projected gap to 1st is about 6 points (737 to 743). Closing it comes down to your cold shooters: Wyatt Johnston, Sam Reinhart and Brady Tkachuk have 35 shots between them and no goals.

Kaprizov drove the week with 5 points, including a hat trick against Florida, and Dylan Holloway had a three-assist night. Kaprizov's 6 goals on 13 shots are running hot, while Frondell lost his top power-play spot and Reinhart is centring a line without Barkov.
Next week, watch Sanderson's return from his lower-body injury, whether Johnston and Reinhart finally score, and Dom Scavuzzo's Hagel and Kucherov, who had 6 points each this week.

recap.text: Chugalugs91 still lead the real standings with 76 points, ahead of Debits & Checks (59) and Peter Will Probably Pick Old Guys (58). Sebastian Aho just set a pool record with a point in six straight games. The projections still have Chugalugs91 finishing last, with a 0.1% title chance.
recap.impact: No threat to you. They lead you by 47 points today, but you're projected to finish about 99 points ahead of them.

recap.text: The title race is a three-way dead heat. Dom Scavuzzo jumped from 4th to 1st projected, with odds up from 11% to 18%. 97 Problems slipped to 2nd at 17%, and Lord of the Rinks sits 3rd at 17%. Debits & Checks are next at 9%.
recap.impact: You're right in it: about 6 projected points separate you from 1st, and the gap to 4th is about 15 points.

recap.text: Biggest movers: PhilCap fell from 3rd to 5th projected (9% to 8%) with Ivan Demidov and William Eklund both on injured reserve. Anthony Scavuzzo dropped from 11th to 14th after Travis Konecny and Mats Zuccarello went on injured reserve. In the real standings, Debits & Checks climbed from 9th to 2nd and RDR slid from 3rd to 10th.
recap.impact: Good for you. PhilCap was one of the teams projected just behind you a week ago, and now sits about 16 points back.

recap.text: Top pool scorers this week: Auston Matthews 9 points (Girl on the Lake), William Nylander 8 (Debits & Checks), and Alexis Lafreniere, Tim Stutzle and Sebastian Aho with 7 each. Dom Scavuzzo got 6 apiece from Brandon Hagel and Nikita Kucherov.
recap.impact: Hagel and Kucherov are the ones that hurt: they powered the team that just passed you. Kaprizov's 5 points led your roster.

recap.text: Role changes on your roster: Anton Frondell dropped from Chicago's top power-play unit to the second, Porter Martone moved up to Philadelphia's second line but back to the second power-play unit, and Brady Tkachuk moved onto Florida's top line. Sam Reinhart is centring Florida's second line with Aleksander Barkov out 6 to 8 weeks.
recap.impact: Small knocks for Frondell and Reinhart, who were already projected for modest totals. Martone's bigger even-strength role is a mild plus.

recap.text: Injuries: Jake Sanderson is still day-to-day with a lower-body injury and has played one game. Travis Konecny and Mats Zuccarello joined the injured reserve list, and Connor Bedard, Ryan Nugent-Hopkins and Mathew Barzal remain out.
recap.impact: Sanderson is the one to watch for you: he has one game played, and every game he misses is one fewer from your defence.

recap.impact: Two of last week's closest chasers stalled, which helps us. The catch is that 97 Problems used the same week to jump past us.

recap.text: Mark Scheifele had the best week in the pool with 10 points for Tage Against the Machine. Mitch Marner (Peter Will Probably Pick Old Guys) and Mikael Granlund (Poppy's Picks) added 8 each, and Connor McDavid ran his pool-record point streak to 16 games for 97 Problems.
recap.impact: Kaprizov led us with 6 and we scored 31 as a team, close to 97 Problems (32) and Tage Against the Machine (33). We didn't lose ground on scoring so much as on Point's absence.

recap.text: Colorado lost Nathan MacKinnon (out at least a month) and Cale Makar (about two weeks), and Montreal's Chris Kreider is out 6 to 8 weeks. Bo Horvat is day-to-day after leaving Saturday's game. Our Brayden Point is still on injured reserve with no timeline.
recap.impact: MacKinnon, Kreider and Horvat all belong to Peter Will Probably Pick Old Guys, who are projected 10th, so those don't change the race. Point does: he's our top-line centre and every week he misses costs us real ground on 97 Problems.

recap.text: On the power play, Mason Marchment moved up to San Jose's first unit, Shane Pinto to Ottawa's and Artturi Lehkonen to Colorado's with MacKinnon and Makar out. For us, Porter Martone is still on Philadelphia's top unit, while Dylan Holloway (now on St. Louis's top line) and Anton Frondell are on second units.
recap.impact: Marchment's bump gives 97 Problems a small boost. On our side it's a wash: Martone's top-unit role offsets Holloway and Frondell playing on the second units.

lens.headline: Thomas and Kaprizov carry the Rinks to the top of the projections.
bullets: We are 3rd in the real standings with 240 points, 7 behind 97 Problems and 5 behind Tage Against the Machine, and projected to finish 1st on about 788 points.
Win odds rose from 21.0% to 29.1% this week, and top-3 odds from 47.6% to 60.0%.
The projected race with 97 Problems is razor thin (about 788 to 786), and Tage are about 20 points further back, so simply keeping pace with 97 Problems in the real standings is what it takes.

Robert Thomas (10 points) and Kirill Kaprizov (8) drove the week. Kaprizov, Brady Tkachuk and Roope Hintz are scoring on more of their shots than usual, so expect some cooling, while Wyatt Johnston is due for more goals. Porter Martone moved up to the top power-play unit; Dylan Holloway and Anton Frondell moved down.
Next week, watch Frondell's status, Nikolaj Ehlers' injury on the 97 Problems side, and whether Aleksander Barkov returns Wednesday alongside Sam Reinhart.

recap.text: 97 Problems take over 1st in the real standings with 247 points after a 44-point week, edging Tage Against the Machine (245), who slip to 2nd. Lord of the Rinks sit 3rd with 240 and Matthew's Team are 4th with 239, so the top four are separated by eight points.
recap.impact: We are 7 points off the lead in the real standings, close enough that one good week flips it. The real race is with 97 Problems.

recap.text: Lord of the Rinks are now the projected favourite, finishing on about 788 points to 97 Problems' 786. Title odds: Lord of the Rinks 29.1%, 97 Problems 25.6%, Tage Against the Machine 13.2%, Dom Scavuzzo 9.8%, PhilCap 8.2%.
recap.impact: Our win odds jumped from 21.0% to 29.1% this week and we passed 97 Problems for 1st in the projections. It is basically a two-horse race with them.

recap.text: Biggest movers: Tage Against the Machine climb from 5th to 3rd in the projections (10.3% to 13.2%), while PhilCap drop from 3rd to 5th (12.8% to 8.2%) and Debits & Checks fall from 4th to 6th (11.4% to 5.4%). Peter Will Probably Pick Old Guys managed only 15 points and tumble from 5th to 10th in the real standings.
recap.impact: PhilCap and Debits & Checks fading thins out the chase pack behind us. Tage are the team to watch for 3rd, but they are projected about 20 points behind us.

recap.text: Top pool scorers this week: Robert Thomas, Brock Boeser and Leon Draisaitl with 10 points each, Connor McDavid with 9, and Kirill Kaprizov, Matt Boldy, Patrick Kane and Tyler Bertuzzi with 8. Boeser has a point in 14 straight games.
recap.impact: Two of the week's top five are ours (Thomas and Kaprizov), and they did most of the lifting behind our 39-point week.

recap.text: Injuries: Nathan MacKinnon is now expected to be out about 12 weeks, Oliver Bjorkstrand is out 2 to 3 months, and Quinn Hughes will miss Minnesota's road trip. Nikolaj Ehlers (97 Problems) missed Sunday after a hit, and Anton Frondell left Saturday's game in Calgary and is day-to-day. Aleksander Barkov could return Wednesday.
recap.impact: Frondell is our lowest-projected skater, so a short absence costs little. Ehlers being hurt dents our main rival, and Barkov's return would help Sam Reinhart's line.

recap.text: Role changes on the lineup sheets: Porter Martone has moved up to the first power-play unit in Philadelphia, while Dylan Holloway in St. Louis and Anton Frondell in Chicago have dropped to the second unit.
recap.impact: Mixed for us: Martone's bump helps, Holloway's drop hurts a little, and Frondell's matters less while he is hurt.

items.headline: Tage Against the Machine seize 1st
items.body: A 12-point night, led by Viktor Arvidsson's three, puts them atop the real standings at 260. Title odds jump to 20%.

items.headline: Johnston won't leave the scoresheet
items.body: Wyatt Johnston scored again in Dallas's loss to Nashville. That's six straight games with a point, six points in all.

items.headline: Vintage Kane hits six straight
items.body: Patrick Kane set up a Roman Kantserov goal in Seattle, making it 9 points over his last six games.

items.headline: Morrissey finds the net in Boston
items.body: Josh Morrissey scored in Winnipeg's 4-2 win, his sixth straight game with a point.
